extracted.intended_audience: graduate or advanced undergraduate students studying commutative algebra; instructors preparing lectures/notes
extracted.subtask_short: assessing ring properties in commutative algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply formal definitions, characterizations, and theorems used to decide/verify algebraic properties of rings and modules (e.g., dimension, Noetherian/Artinian, Jacobson, associated primes, primary decomposition). Useful for proving or checking these properties in examples and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull dimension (dim(R))
rubrics_metrics.description: dim(R) is defined to be the supremum of the lengths r of all strictly ascending chains of prime ideals p0 ⫋ p1 ⫋ ... ⫋ pr in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chains of prime ideals to compute or compare dimensions. For a finitely generated k-algebra domain R, dim(R) = trdeg_k(Frac(R)). Corollaries: for a prime p in such an R, dim(R_p) + dim(R/p) = dim(R); if p is maximal then dim(R_p) = dim(R). Catenary property (for finitely generated k-algebras) implies all maximal chains between two primes have the same length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether Normalization (structure & dimension reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a finitely generated k-algebra (domain) then there exists a polynomial subring P = k[t1,...,tm] such that R is module-finite over P, and m = trdeg_k(Frac(P)) = trdeg_k(Frac(R)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noether Normalization provides a polynomial subring over which R is integral/finite; it yields equality of transcendence degree and Krull dimension in the finitely generated domain case and is used to compare chains of primes via contractions to P. Use incomparability/going-down arguments after normalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catenary property for finitely generated algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring R is catenary if for any nested primes q ⫋ p there exists a chain of primes of maximal length from q to p and any two such maximal chains have the same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over a field, any finitely generated algebra is catenary. Use reduction to a domain (R/q) and Noether Normalization / dimension arguments to check lengths of chains through a given prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Jacobson ring
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring R is Jacobson if for every ideal a, its radical equals the intersection of all maximal ideals containing a: rad(a) = ∩_{m ⊇ a} m. Equivalently, it suffices that this equality holds whenever a is prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topological reformulation: Spec(R) is Jacobson iff closed points are very dense (closed points meet every nonempty locally closed subset). Examples: fields, polynomial rings k[X1,...,Xn], Z, k[X]. Properties: quotients of Jacobson rings are Jacobson; integral finite extensions of a Jacobson ring are Jacobson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent condition for Jacobson rings (prime/localization test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring R is Jacobson iff for any nonmaximal prime p and any f not in p, the extension pR_f is not maximal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this localization criterion to test Jacobson property. It yields consequences such as the Generalized Hilbert Nullstellensatz: in a Jacobson base ring, contractions of maximal ideals from a finitely generated algebra are maximal and residue fields are algebraic over the base residue field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalized Hilbert Nullstellensatz (over Jacobson rings)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Jacobson and R' is a finitely generated R-algebra, and m' is a maximal ideal of R' with contraction m in R, then (1) m is maximal and R'/m' is algebraic over R/m, and (2) R' is Jacobson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply by reducing to R/m and using algebraicity/integrality arguments: finite generation and field quotient force algebraic finite field extension. Use to deduce behavior of maximal ideals in polynomial rings over Jacobson bases and arithmetic consequences (Z and polynomial rings over fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian ring (definition and equivalent chain conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring R is Noetherian if every ideal is finitely generated. Equivalently, R satisfies the ascending chain condition (ACC) on ideals, or every nonempty set of ideals has a maximal element under inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ACC, maximal condition, or explicit finite generation to verify Noetherian property. Examples: PID, polynomial ring k[X] (one variable), Z. Non-examples: polynomial ring in infinitely many variables, certain subrings exhibiting infinite strictly increasing ideal chains. Proof techniques often use generating sets and stabilization of chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert Basis Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Noetherian then the polynomial ring R[X] is Noetherian (and by induction R[X1,...,Xn] is Noetherian). Consequently any finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use degree-leading-coefficient argument: given an ideal in R[X], choose minimal-degree representatives to show the ideal of leading coefficients is finitely generated in R, then finite generation of the polynomial ideal follows. Apply to deduce Noetherian property of quotients and finitely generated algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's theorem (primes generating Noetherianity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring is Noetherian if every prime ideal is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Zorn's lemma: a maximal non-finitely-generated ideal must be prime, contradiction. This gives a practical test: if you can show all primes are finitely generated, the whole ring is Noetherian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian module (definition and equivalent conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-module M is Noetherian if every submodule is finitely generated, equivalently M satisfies ACC on submodules or every nonempty set of submodules has a maximal element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact sequences: M is Noetherian iff submodule N and quotient M/N are Noetherian. Finite direct sums: finite direct sums of Noetherian modules are Noetherian. Over a Noetherian ring, a module is Noetherian iff it is finitely generated; moreover, finitely generated modules are finitely presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence over Noetherian ring: finitely generated ⇔ Noetherian ⇔ finitely presented
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Noetherian and M an R-module, then M is Noetherian iff M is finitely generated iff M is finitely presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that R^n is Noetherian and that kernels of surjections from finite free modules are finitely generated; this yields finite presentation. Conversely finite presentation or Noetherianity implies finite generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artinian module/ring (definition & basic consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: A module (or ring) is Artinian if it satisfies the descending chain condition (DCC) on submodules (ideals). The equivalent minimal condition (minc) is that every nonempty set of submodules has a minimal element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: an Artinian domain is a field; every prime ideal in an Artinian ring is maximal. Finite-dimensional k-algebras (as vector spaces) are both Noetherian and Artinian. Behavior under short exact sequences parallels Noetherian case: M Artinian iff N and M/N Artinian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prime ideal p is associated to an R-module M if there exists a nonzero m in M with Ann(m) = p. The set of associated primes is denoted Ass(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent formulation: p ∈ Ass(M) iff there exists an R-injection R/p ↪ M. Distinguish minimal associated primes (minimal elements of Ass(M)) and embedded primes. For ideals a, consider associated primes of R/a (convention in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and associated primes relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: For any module M, Ass(M) ⊆ Supp(M). For Noetherian modules, Supp(M) = ⋃_{q ∈ Ass(M)} V(q) (so every prime in the support contains some associated prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use localization: p ∈ Supp(M) iff M_p ≠ 0 and then show M_p has an associated prime coming from Ass(M). Minimal elements of Supp(M) are associated primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness of associated primes for finitely generated modules over Noetherian rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Noetherian and M is finitely generated, then Ass(M) is a finite set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a finite filtration with cyclic quotients R/p_i (Lemma 17.19) to show Ass(M) ⊆ {p1,...,pn}. Use this when analyzing zerodivisors and primary decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zerodivisor characterization via associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian ring R and module M, the set of zerodivisors on M equals the union of associated primes: zdiv(M) = ⋃_{p ∈ Ass(M)} p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To see x is a zerodivisor, find m ≠ 0 with xm = 0; then Ann(m) is contained in some maximal annihilator which is associated. Conversely, any element of an associated prime annihilates some element, hence is a zerodivisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization behavior of associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: If p ∈ Ass(M) and S is a multiplicative set with p ∩ S = ∅, then the localization S^{-1}p ∈ Ass(S^{-1}M). Conversely, if S^{-1}p is associated to S^{-1}M and p is finitely generated then p ∈ Ass(M) (and necessarily p ∩ S = ∅).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the injection R/p ↪ M and localize; conversely lift annihilators back using finite generation and clearing denominators. This is a practical tool to move Ass information between R and localizations R_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary submodule / primary ideal (definition & equivalent characterizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A submodule Q of M is p-primary if Ass(M/Q) = {p}. For a Noetherian ring and finitely generated module M, equivalent characterizations include: (i) p = nil(M/Q) is prime; (ii) zdiv(M/Q) = p; (iii) if x ∈ R and m ∈ M with x m ∈ Q but m ∉ Q then x ∈ p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ideals q ⊂ R: q is p-primary iff whenever xy ∈ q and x ∉ sqrt(q) then y ∈ sqrt(q) (so nilradical of R/q is prime). Use these criteria to detect primary components and to verify p-primary property by testing zerodivisors and nilpotents in the quotient.
